title: CVE-2019-5481: krb5: double-free in read_data() after realloc() fail
explain: The real code shows the flaw the report describes.
summary: Double-free of 'buf->data' occurs in lib/security.c's teardown path when Curl_saferealloc() fails, potentially exploitable via remote trigger of realloc() failure with len=0x7fffffff.

claims.text: double-free of the reference 'buf->data' on the teardown path if 'Curl_saferealloc()' fails
claims.reasoning: When Curl_saferealloc fails with non-zero size, it frees the original pointer (buf->data) and returns NULL. read_data then returns an error code without nulling buf->data. The caller's teardown path will subsequently free buf->data a second time, causing a double-free.

citations.note: Curl_saferealloc(buf->data, len) called; on failure it frees buf->data and returns NULL
Curl_saferealloc frees ptr when size != 0 and realloc fails
read_data returns CURLE_OUT_OF_MEMORY without setting buf->data = NULL, leaving dangling pointer

claims.reasoning: The read_data function is located in lib/security.c as shown in the provided source.

claims.text: sender might be able to remotely trigger a realloc() failure ... by sending the value 0x7fffffff
claims.reasoning: The len value is read directly from the network socket, converted from network byte order, and passed to Curl_saferealloc. An attacker controlling the network stream can send 0x7fffffff (2,147,483,647), which on a 32-bit system will likely cause realloc to fail due to address space exhaustion.

citations.note: len read from socket via socket_read(fd, &len, sizeof(len))
len = ntohl(len) converts network byte order to host order
len passed to Curl_saferealloc as size argument

claims.text: double-free after a 'realloc()' failure, which could be triggered remotely
claims.reasoning: Combines C1 and C3: attacker-controlled len can trigger realloc failure, leading to double-free on teardown.

citations.note: Attacker controls len via network input
Curl_saferealloc frees original buffer on allocation failure
buf->data not nulled before error return

claims.text: realloc failure with particular 'len' value can be reproduced ... by sending the value 0x7fffffff
claims.reasoning: The reporter's test case demonstrates that realloc(0x7fffffff) fails on a 32-bit system. Since len comes from the network and is passed directly to realloc via Curl_saferealloc, the same failure can be triggered in the actual code path.

citations.note: len = ntohl(len) - attacker-controlled value reaches realloc

key_reasons: Curl_saferealloc frees the original pointer on realloc failure (lib/strdup.c:96-98)
read_data returns error without setting buf->data = NULL (lib/security.c:206-207)
len is read from attacker-controlled network socket (lib/security.c:197)
0x7fffffff is a plausible trigger on 32-bit systems causing allocation failure
Double-free on teardown is a security-relevant heap corruption vulnerability
reply: Thank you for the report. The double-free in read_data() is confirmed: when Curl_saferealloc fails, it frees buf->data but read_data returns without nulling the pointer, leaving a dangling reference that will be freed again on teardown. The len value is read from the network, so an attacker can trigger this on 32-bit systems by sending 0x7fffffff. We will fix this by ensuring buf->data is set to NULL on allocation failure.
